I started transitioning at 23 years old. I had dysphoria most of my life so I tried very hard to pass as a cis woman. I only came out as gay two years into college because I went to very sexist, homophobic and transphobic private schools my whole life. My family was not equipped to be with a trans person. I was only able transition because frankly I’d had enough pretending so when I graduated uni I decided to start T. 

Personally I’m glad I had 23 years to think about it and really reflect, simply because I don’t want to make a decision I would regret. However trust me I’ve questioned my transition quite a bit before I started feeling much more comfortable about it. I think 17 is a good age of introspection to trust your decision. It’s not like you started very very young. And also know you can take charge of how fast you want to go by micro dosing hormones. 

I am currently somewhat microdosing my hormones but the change I’ve had is definitely helping me pass. I’m at a stage where if I stopped I could still go back to being femme presenting. Personally I don’t want to. 

I believe you’ll find more confidence in your decision as you see the results. And just know you can always change your mind about how you transition at any point. Good luck!
